For coarse cellular eutectic alloy, the bonding strength of eutectic cell boundary was very weak, and the area of cell boundary was large, crack was easy to initiate and propagate at the cell boundary.

If the solidification microstructure contained coarse primary Cr(Mo) dendrit es phase, the bonding strength between the Cr(Mo) dendritic phase and the eutectic phase wa s very poor, and the arrangement of eutectic lamellae near the Cr(Mo) dendrites was disordered. Crack nucleation and propagation were extremely easy, and eventually leading to fracture of alloy under low loading, so the NiAl-36Cr-6Mo alloy solidified at 10 μm/s had the lowest tensile strength and elongation.

Due to the fast withdrawal rate, eutectic microstructure was refined, the perfect cellular eutectic alloy possessed higher tensile strength and moderate elongation, both higher than planar eutectic alloy.

For perfect cellular alloy, the bonding strength between eutectic cells was high, which resulted in high crack propagation resistance and harmonious deformation in the intracellular regions and the intercellular regions , so a ll the above strengthening mechanisms could work.
